events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph's pier.** Rating **1 (below average)**. It's the only one of the four with a pier report above 0 in the last few weeks.
- **Fish spawn on the bottom.** The most recent St. Joseph pier report (Apr 26) said pier anglers were catching a few coho on spawn fished on the bottom.
- **South Haven and Muskegon: rating 0 (slow).** Both had slow pier reports on Apr 26.
- **Grand Haven: rating 0 to 1.** No pier-specific report is recent enough to rate it confidently. Treat it as slow for now.

## Why

- **St. Joseph is the best of a slow group.** The Apr 26 St. Joseph report had the only pier catch above 0 this spring, though it was still rated below average (St. Joseph, 2023-04-26).
- **Muskegon and South Haven were slow last week.** Both reported pier anglers doing poorly on Apr 26 (Muskegon, 2023-04-26; South Haven, 2023-04-26).
- **I'd expect slow pier fishing to continue for a while.** Past years at similar water temperatures (about 46 F) also had mostly slow to below-average pier reports (past seasons, late April to early May).

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Apr 26, about 6 days old)
- St. Joseph, 2023-04-26: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho using spawn fished on the bottom." Rated 1. Boat anglers did better in 10 to 60 feet of water on crankbaits and small spoons.
- South Haven, 2023-04-26: "Pier fishing was slow for coho." Rated 0.
- Muskegon, 2023-04-26: "Pier anglers found the action to be very slow for brown trout and coho salmon." Rated 0.
- Grand Haven, 2023-04-20: "Dirty water from the Grand River has slowed the action for brown trout and coho salmon." No pier method given. Grand Haven's last pier-specific report was 2023-04-12, rated 1, with coho on spawn and orange spoons. That report is three weeks old.

**Past seasons** (general history, not current)
- Reports from late April and early May with surface water within 4 F of 46 F were mostly pier-slow or below average. South Haven and St. Joseph ratings were 0 to 1 (South Haven, 2022-04-20 and 2022-05-04; St. Joseph, 2022-04-20, 2022-04-27 and 2022-05-04).
- Boats usually did better than the pier in those years. At St. Joseph, boats got a 3 on 2022-05-04 at 50 F surface water, fishing 30 feet deep for coho.

**Conditions now**
- Measured buoy surface water (this is the week before May 2, since live data was unavailable):
  - St. Joseph: 46 F, flat over the week.
  - South Haven: 46 F, down 1 F.
  - Grand Haven and Muskegon: 45 F, down 3 F.
- I did not get modeled pierhead water or the wind forecast, so I can't check for upwelling at the piers.

## Caveats

- **The reports are old.** The newest is Apr 26, about 6 days before today, so this is a guide, not a live report.
- **The water data is partly old.** The buoy readings are from the week before May 2, not today, and I have no pierhead water data.
- **Grand Haven's pier rating is weak.** Its newest report is 12 days old and not pier-specific.
- **Surface water is cool.** At 45 to 46 F, all four ports sit below the 52 to 58 F range that Chinook and coho generally prefer (NY DEC reference), so the bite may depend on upwelling or on the fish moving in.

## Sources

- Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph reports, 2023-04-26: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3573537
- Grand Haven, Muskegon reports, 2023-04-20: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3561fa6
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph reports, 2023-04-12: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3548e2b
- Past season comparisons: 2022-05-04 (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173), 2022-04-27 (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3155afc), 2022-04-20 (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3145666)
